Venus Introduction



“The future of finance isn’t just built in banks but through through innovation.”

As technology continues to revolunise how we interact with money, I’m deeply fascinated by the intersection of finance and technology and together with AI, it is redefining accessibility, innovation, and trust within the financial ecosystem. From algorithmic trading to decentralized finance, I believe the next generation of finance will work hand-in-hand with AI, data, and automation using intelligent systems that learn and predict, creating a world where financial decisions are faster and smarter to all.

Currently, I’m pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree (Hons) in Applied Computing at SIT, after graduating with a Diploma in Computer Engineering from Singapore Polytechnic (Specialized in Software and Hardware). My academic journey has built a strong foundation in problem-solving, systems thinking, and innovation, allowing me to explore how technology can reshape financial infrastructures.

I’m proficient in various programming languages such as Python, JavaScript, CSS, C, and Java, which supports development across both front-end and back-end. Additionally, I am well-versed in digital marketing strategies, including SEO, social media marketing, and content marketing, to drive brand awareness and customer acquisition.

I am a firm believer in continuous self-growth. I’m passionate about investing and in my free time, I actively upskill with Udemy, where I’m currently enrolled into a 56-hour course on AI Automations with n8n as well as Financial Analyst Training & Investing program. These courses have expanded my understanding of applied AI automation and financial intelligence.

When I’m free, I love to dive into books (fiction and non-fiction), 2 books that have profoundly shaped how I think and live are The Psychology of Money by Morgan Housel, which changed how I view wealth, behavior, and long-term decision-making, and Man’s Search for Meaning by Viktor Frankl, which taught me resilience, purpose, and perspective.

title: About
text:
Automating Bookkeeping with AI and n8n
I built an AI Automated Bookkeeping System using n8n, OpenAI, Telegram, and Google Drive/Sheets to automatically sort invoices, extracting details, and updating spreadsheets.

Features:

Telegram Upload: send an invoice (PDF or image) to a Telegram bot I created


File Detection & Extraction: n8n detects the file type, extracts text using built-in PDF/image processing


AI Processing (OpenAI GPT-4o): the extracted text is passed to OpenAI, which parses key accounting data like invoice number, vendor name, invoice date & due date, description of services, subtotal, tax, total, and payment status


Data Parsing & Formatting: A JavaScript node cleans and structures the AI output into JSON format


Cloud Storage & Record Keeping: The invoice is automatically uploaded to Google Drive, shared publicly, and its link is saved


Google Sheets Update: the extracted information and the invoice file link are appended to a live Google Sheet database automatically



What It Solves:

Eliminates manual data entry
Saves hours of repetitive bookkeeping
Centralizes invoice records with attached files
Reduces human error in financial data logging
Enables real-time expense tracking

title: Reflection on the use of GenAI
section: How did the GenAI tool help me in completing the assessment?
text:
How did the GenAI tool help me in completing the assessment?
I had issues with the Github commit and push as I was not familiar with the interface here and did not connect my github to the terminal properly. I used ChatGPT to help me with the commands needed to connect my github to the terminal and push my code successfully.

title: Reflection on the use of GenAI
section: What do I think are challenging about the tool?
text:
What do I think are challenging about the tool?
In terms of the overall usability, ChatGPT is by far the most unreliable when it comes to calculating long mathematical equations as compared to coding.
However, in terms of this module, I believe that the challenge is showing the errors and issues with the interface, as I am still learning about the RStudio interface, without the ChatGPT pro (I am not able to send as many pictures as I would like)

title: Reflection on the use of GenAI
section: How do I think GenAI tool assis me for my future study or work?
text:
How do I think GenAI tool assis me for my future study or work?
I believe that GenAI tools will help in the efficiency in work and studies instead of taking over my job as a student or worker. Ultimately, I still have to put in effort in understanding my tasks, what I am stuck with, and fact check the information provided by ChatGPT.

As the world evolves, I believe we have to evolve as well and adapt to the new technology. Learning how to use GenAI tools effectively will be a great skill to have in the future.

I have linked an article on the GenAI impact on humans here, where the article by Deloitte. states that “Despite all the hype, it’s not meant to replace humans, but to better unlock human potential”, which I agree with.
